title: Martin Heidegger — Why You Feel It, And Who Decided #Shorts
description:
The story Martin Heidegger tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Martin Heidegger (26 September 1889 – 26 May 1976) was a German philosopher whose work was central to the development of phenomenology, hermeneutics, and existentialism. Heidegger's magnum opus, Being and Time (1927), is widely considered one of the most significant works of modern philosophy.

Strip Martin Heidegger of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Heidegger modifies traditional ontology by focusing instead on the meaning of being. This kind of ontological inquiry, he claims, is required to understand the basis of our understanding, scientific and otherwise.

scenes.narration: The story Martin Heidegger tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Martin Heidegger (26 September
1889 – 26 May 1976) was a German philosopher whose work was central to the development of phenomenology,
hermeneutics, and existentialism. Heidegger's magnum opus, Being and Time (1927), is widely considered one of the most significant
works of modern philosophy. Meaning is not found in Martin Heidegger — it is manufactured for it. In
it, he introduced the concept of Dasein ("being-there") to describe the distinctive character of human existence, arguing that
humans possess a "pre-ontological" understanding of being that shapes how they live and act, which he analyzed in
terms of the unitary structure of "being-in-the-world".
